title: Flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry of the mouse dural meninges for immunological and virological assessments
protocol: Euthanize the mouse using an intraperitoneal injection of ketamine and xylazine cocktail.
Wait for the mouse to become unresponsive to a toe pinch.
Place the mouse on its back and pin each limb down to the dissection board.
Spray ethanol 70% on the mouse abdomen to clean the area.
Open the mouse abdomen with scissors, cutting up to the thorax.
Carefully expose the heart without cutting any major blood vessels.
Make a cut in the right atrium to allow blood flow out of the heart.
Inject the left ventricle of the heart with ice-cold PBS using a 20 mL syringe equipped with a 23G x 1 inch needle.
Continue perfusion until the liver has whitened.
Decapitate the mouse.
Using scissors, cut and remove the scalp until the skull is fully visible.
Cut the skull in the longitudinal plane from the back of the head to the nose without damaging the brain.
Extract the skull cap gently without difficulty.
Gently extract the brain and dural meninges using fine-tipped forceps without scraping the inside of the skull.
Ensure that the entire dura is extracted, avoiding bone or brain tissue.
Keep the dural meninges hydrated with PBS 1× frequently.
Digest the meningeal tissue in an enzymatic mix at 37°C for 30 minutes in a water bath.
Gently shake the tube every 10 minutes during digestion.
Stop the digestion after 30 minutes.
Dissociate the tissue by performing 20 recurrent aspirations through a 1,000 μL tip.
Pass the cellular suspension through a 35-μm pore cell strainer capped tube.
Spin at 450 g at 4°C for 2 minutes.
Remove most of the supernatant and leave 200 μL of cell suspension.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 96-well bottom plate.
Wash the cells twice with 100 μL of FACS Buffer (spin at 450 g at 4°C for 2 minutes, then remove supernatant).
Stain the cells with the viability marker for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Wash the stained cells with FACS Buffer (spin at 450 g at 4°C for 2 minutes, then remove supernatant).
Block the cell suspension with 50 μL of blocking solution for 10 minutes on ice.
Add 50 μL of antibody cocktail (diluted 2×) and incubate for 30 minutes in the dark.
Wash the cells twice with FACS Buffer (spin at 450 g at 4°C for 2 minutes, then remove supernatant).
Resuspend the cells in 150 μL of FACS Buffer.
Acquire the samples on a compatible cytometer.
Fix the skull containing the dural meninges for 10 min with formalin 5% at 25°C.
Wash the sample three times with 1 mL of PBS 1×, leaving each wash for 1 min.
Incubate dural meninges in 1.5 mL of blocking solution at 25°C for 15 min.
Extract gently the meninges from the skull with fine-tipped forceps.
Spread out and flatten the meninges on a glass slide in PBS 1×.
Circle the meninges with a hydrophobic pen to keep the solution from spreading on the slide.
Stain the meninges with the primary antibody mix using the purified rat anti-LCMV antibody for 12 hours at 4°C.
Wash the meninges 3 times with 200 μL of PBS 1×. Each wash should be left for 1 minute.
Stain the meninges with the secondary antibody goat anti-rat Alexa Fluor 568 for 2 hours at 25°C.
Wash the meninges 3 times with 200 μL of PBS 1×. Each wash should be left for 1 minute.
Mount the meninges with a cover-slip and mounting medium.
Put a dot of nail polish at each corner of the cover-slip to stabilize it.
Let the meninges dry at 25°C for 2 hours before imaging.
